text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: C:/Users/ryanf/github/TODO/pixel-lab-docsuite/build/authority-projects/pixl-host-trial-cbs6n8uw/APPROACH.md
+Propose one small lantern with dark structural framing, teal glass, a restrained warm light, intentional partial transparency, and selectively authored anti-aliasing. A front-facing 32 × 32 RGBA sample is a useful starting experiment because it permits comparison with the reference at the same logical scale. Its dimensions, design, colors, and lighting are proposals; matching quality remains to be demonstrated.
+
+This is the Markdown approach requested on 2026-09-14. Work performed comprised reference inspection, read-only local PIXL measurements and method research, and writing this document. No project PX2 state was initialized or amended, no production art was created, and no provider was called. All lantern authoring and review steps below are future work.
+
+I viewed [translucent-reference.png](translucent-reference.png) at native dimensions and inspected an in-memory 12× nearest-neighbor enlargement composited over light `#F0F0F0`, dark `#181820`, and checkerboard `#888888`/`#CCCCCC` backgrounds. These diagnostic backgrounds are not established game backgrounds. The image has a blocky dark frame, two upright top extensions, a broad teal interior, and two pale warm rectangular details. Narrow translucent teal strips run beside the dark sides. On the inspected dark background the frame has less separation, while the side strips remain visible; their appearance changes on the light background. This does not establish readability on arbitrary scenes or a contrast threshold.
+
+The measured reference is a single 32 × 32 RGBA frame. Of its 1,024 pixels, 604 have alpha 0, 390 have alpha 255, 15 have alpha 96, and 15 have alpha 160. The fractional pixels are teal `#56B5BC`: the left strip is at zero-based x=6, y=11–25 with alpha 96; the right is at x=25, y=11–25 with alpha 160. The nonzero-alpha bounding box is `[6,3,26,28)` and there is one component under four-neighbor connectivity. The three visible RGB colors are dark blue `#25354A`, teal `#56B5BC`, and pale yellow `#F4DDA2`; PIXL reports five visible color entries because teal occurs at three alpha levels. These counts and coordinates describe this file only.
+
+The user explicitly identifies the treatment as intentional partial transparency and selective anti-aliasing. The straight side strips could also read as a rim or glow, but that interpretation does not replace either requested treatment. The reference supplies limited evidence for how a curved lantern handle should be softened. That uncertainty calls for testing the curve while preserving both treatments.
+
+Authority is carried into every proposed instruction and check as follows:
+
+| Property / value | Status and owner | Exact source | Applicable scope |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Small matching lantern | Requirement, user | “prepare a production approach for a small matching lantern prop” | Subject and reference relationship |
+| Intentional partial transparency and selective anti-aliasing | Requirement, user | “uses intentional partial transparency and selective anti-aliasing. Keep that treatment in the new props.” | Lantern authoring, export, and visual review |
+| No fixed palette restriction | Current brief, user | “I have not imposed a fixed palette.” | No exact RGB/RGBA membership gate or color-count limit |
+| Markdown only; no state, art, or provider action | Requirement, user | “The requested deliverable is this Markdown approach only; do not initialize or amend PX2 state, create production art, or call a provider.” | This evaluation |
+| Reference dimensions, colors, alpha levels, bounds, connectivity | Measurements, local tools | Exact reference bytes and measurements above | Reference description only; no copied numerical rejection rules |
+| Dark framing, teal field, warm accents, selective edge softness | Visual observations, assistant | Native reference and the specified 12× background views | Evidence informing a style proposal; not exact geometry or lighting requirements |
+| 32 × 32, front-facing static lantern; loop, cap, glass chamber, base | Proposal, assistant | Same-scale comparison and recognizable lantern landmarks | First sample experiment; final size, projection, and design remain open |
+| Teal glass, opaque frame, small warm core; optional extra ramp colors | Proposal, assistant | Adaptation of the observed color roles | Sample shading and material experiment; no fixed swatch list |
+| Partial alpha on glass margins; AA on selected handle/cap transitions | Proposal implementing the user's treatment | User treatment requirement plus the selected PIXL methods below | Candidate-specific placement, adjustable with the lantern shape |
+| Straight-alpha PNG master, point-sampled inspection, background round trip | Technical proposal, assistant | PIXL `alpha-contract` and `selective-edge-aa`; reference inspection | Sample/export experiment; target renderer behavior remains unverified |
+| Display size, scene backgrounds, engine/import path, placement anchor | Unresolved | Not specified in the supplied brief or SESSION.md | Final production and destination review |
+
+For later production, use this sequence:
+
+1. Establish the intended on-screen size and placement context. Start the proposed sample at 32 × 32 if a same-scale experiment is useful; do not infer that this is a required canvas or a minimum viable size. Use the intended game projection when supplied. A centered composition with a base anchor is a trial choice until hanging, standing, or inventory use is known.
+2. Block a loop handle, cap, framed glass chamber, and base with enough separation to read as a lantern at native size. Keep broad clusters and limited decorative detail in the spirit of the reference. Explore the curved handle even though the reference mostly has straight edges. Its precise contour, gap width, and component count remain design choices.
+3. Shade by material role: dark structural metal, teal glass, and a small pale warm light inside. Propose a centrally lit chamber rather than infer a directional light from the reference's two bright details or unequal side alpha. Additional hue/value steps are available when they help form or edge transitions. A fixed-palette study is optional and is not a prerequisite.
+4. Author real fractional alpha in selected glass margins and narrow edge transitions, retaining enough opaque structure to support the form. Test additional pane translucency only where it helps the glass read. Author selective anti-aliasing separately at chosen handle bends and cap shoulders using deliberate intermediate color and/or coverage pixels. Keep contrasting hard structural edges where the sample design calls for them. A glow alone does not satisfy selective AA, and colored AA on a wholly opaque sprite does not satisfy partial transparency. Selectivity means intentional placement; the chosen regions can change with the design.
+5. Preserve authored RGBA values through export. Propose a straight-alpha PNG master and nearest-neighbor diagnostic views so individual edge decisions can be inspected. If the destination consumes premultiplied alpha, test the conversion and blend behavior there. Compare native and enlarged views on light, dark, checkerboard, and the actual scene background. Review the saved/reopened file and, later, its engine import for lost translucency, unwanted matte-colored fringes, or darkening from incorrect alpha handling.
+
+The smallest useful future proof is one lantern containing a curved handle, hard structural edges, a warm interior, and deliberately translucent glass margins. Its question is whether those forms retain the requested selective AA and transparency while reading as a matching lantern at the intended size. If the AA placement is uncertain, compare two localized revisions of that same lantern; both retain fractional alpha and selective AA. No lantern proof has been executed in this evaluation.
+
+Proposed review separates brief requirements from experimental diagnostics:
+
+| Review | Evidence to collect later | Interpretation |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Both requested treatments retained | Fractional-alpha measurements plus visual inspection of named translucent regions and selected AA edges | Loss of either treatment conflicts with the brief. Fractional pixels alone do not prove selective AA quality. |
+| Lantern identity and reference relationship | Native comparison of candidate/reference; inspect handle, chamber, base, cluster scale, frame weight, and material/color relationships | Visual judgment of matching and readability; proposed landmarks guide this design rather than exclude every other lantern design. |
+| Edge behavior across backgrounds | Native and integer-enlarged composites, including the destination scene when available | Assess intentional softness, hard-edge contrast, and unintended fringes. A failure is scoped to that candidate, scale, background, and rendering path. |
+| File mechanics | Decode RGBA, record frame size and alpha distribution; run PIXL asset-check with `alpha: "full"` and omit `palette` | Actual size is recorded; enforce size only after adoption. No binary-alpha rule, exact alpha set, palette membership, component count, or coordinate matching. |
+| Destination preservation | Actual import/export round trip with recorded sampling, alpha handling, and display scale | Establishes behavior only in the tested destination. Unavailable engine review remains unverified. |
+
+If one candidate reads poorly or has a fringe, revise its contour, local alpha, intermediate colors, or import handling while retaining both requested treatments. Retest the affected views. That result would not prove a general minimum canvas, prohibit rounded forms, or establish that a provider cannot produce this style. Provider capability and reliability are untested here; any later provider work would require actual capability discovery and assessment of returned pixels.
+
+For method research, I used the packaged PIXL source inventory, retrieved the exact cited text, loaded the three complete compiled method contexts, and read their bounded receipt entries. The selected methods remain candidates for this project:
+
+| Method | Useful transfer | Prerequisites and evidence limits |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `selective-edge-aa` | Deliberate edge placement and background comparison | The sample needs its own edge regions and suitable colors. The bundled fixture proves two-pixel edit locality and its own palette check, not perceptual AA quality. Its approved-palette and byte-identical-edge conditions are not project-wide requirements here. |
+| `alpha-contract` | Separate opacity from RGB choice; preserve a consistent compositing interpretation | Full alpha is applicable; the recipe's conditional binary-alpha check is inapplicable. Its receipt tests linear numeric blending, not display color management or a GPU/importer. |
+| `silhouette-readability` | Inspect landmark separation and actual colored appearance at target scale | Target size/backgrounds remain unresolved. Its key fixture checks geometry, not lantern recognition. An opaque silhouette preview, if used, is only a diagnostic and cannot replace the translucent candidate. |
+
+Reproducible source identities are retained here rather than in production state. All paths below are within `.agents/skills/pixl-kit/resources/`:
+
+- Reference SHA-256: `bda5c9b18e38b60a617877de6e9df6c5bf8e040410e9dfbe6bc85ca501b17132`. Local `pixl_asset_check` used full alpha and no palette constraint; its mechanical result does not grant visual or engine acceptance.
+- [knowledge/pixel-art.json](.agents/skills/pixl-kit/resources/knowledge/pixel-art.json), methods beginning at lines 157, 306, and 769 respectively for silhouette, AA, and alpha; SHA-256 `d169c546d99f59b4adb4d0a939b61bd7b3d21bc0b3b2e13116e2e10a4882f15c`. Compiled contexts: `knowledge/library.px`, focuses `k.silhouette-readability`, `k.selective-edge-aa`, and `k.alpha-contract`.
+- [PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md](.agents/skills/pixl-kit/resources/training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md), SHA-256 `7efc4789ca70dfd9964abc2bc1100af318306236400e3496f7a0a5654f725e28`: AA citations 590–632 and 907–919; alpha citations 945–977 and 1276–1291; silhouette citations 857–867 and 1563–1573.
+- [PIXEL-ART-ASSETS.md](.agents/skills/pixl-kit/resources/training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-ASSETS.md), SHA-256 `450a335ed6563a7f4a5cc380f2bbe72f98b70e532ac2c8d16a679bcc545d4900`: alpha citation 942–958 and silhouette citation 11–15. These archive passages concern CSS effects and UI context; the alpha research passages concern asset channels/alignment. They do not directly prove this lantern's compositing or readability. The specific compositing and landmark procedures come from the local method recipes and bounded fixtures. Historical external citation tokens were not treated as independently verified current documentation.
+- [evidence/art-methods/poc-report.json](.agents/skills/pixl-kit/resources/evidence/art-methods/poc-report.json), SHA-256 `a3b77eae4ab97843829efab67b8773086498d67d91672350520194059f586d81`, recorded 2026-09-14T13:05:30.131009+00:00. Relevant entries: `selective-aa-boundary`, `alpha-compositing-contract`, and `key-silhouette-landmarks`. These are bundled offline results, not new lantern trials or production acceptance.
+
+The approach is ready for use in a later production task. The next consequential choice is the lantern's intended on-screen size and placement background; those determine whether the proposed 32 × 32 front-facing experiment is representative. Engine and anchor details can follow when the destination is established. No fixed palette decision is needed to preserve the requested aesthetic.
*** End Patch"));
